newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany, France still partners in Europe - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Germany, France still partners in Europe - Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Monday he was convinced that after the left-wing election victory in France the new government would continue the country's support Europe's planned monetary union (EMU).

Kinkel told reporters before a meeting of Free Democrat (FDP) party executives he was sure the planned single currency, euro, would be launched on time and that countries participating would fulfil the criteria precisely.

"Germany and France remain for me the most important partners. We want to go further in Europe. The euro can be launched under strict adherence to the criteria and the planned timetable," Kinkel told reporters.
Kinkel said that although the France-German partnership was still the chief motor behind European economic union, the two countries might have different views on some issues.
"I congratulate the French government on its election victory and thank the outgoing foreign minister Herve de Charette for his cooperation," Kinkel said.
In contrast, German newspapers voiced doubts and concerns about the future of Europe's integration drive, and especially its planned common currency, after the change of government in France.
